title: The porter learns members the game closed, moved or made generic
result: 2026-11-19: port.jar-links.every-update 5,731 -> 5,775 of 9,149 on top of #124 (main measured again on the same runners; before #124 it was 5,302 -> 5,365), no update lower (+12 NeoForge and +9 Fabric on 1.20.6 -> 1.21, +7 on 1.19.2 -> 1.19.3, +6 on 1.19.3 -> 1.19.4, +6 on 1.16.5 -> 1.17). On a real 1.21.1 -> 1.21.2 server 24 of the 27 that link load and 1 is client-only; the other 2 fail on data files 1.21.2 cannot parse. On a real 1.21 server 38 of the 45 that link load, 5 of them through the constructor-to-factory rewrite (WorldEdit 124 times); Explorer's and Nature's Compass fail on ModLoadingContext.registerConfig, a change in NeoForge's loader (FML) whose classes the link check does not read. Next: read FML's classes in the snapshot; then overrides whose parameters changed type, with the new argument passed into the mod's old method.
text: Of the 60 references that hold back the most mods across every update, 25 are members the route map still follows but that no longer work: a constructor made private (new ResourceLocation(ns, path), 99 Fabric mods on 1.20.6 -> 1.21), a field moved to another class (Registry.BLOCK), a field made private behind a getter or setter (Player.inventory, AbstractWidget.y), a method replaced by a generic one. Such a member is learned like a removed one: from its exact public wrapper in the new release (the closed member called with the same arguments, through checks that return them), the accessor whose body only reads or writes it, or what the game's own uses wrote, with readings shown only on literal arguments refused. JarPort turns new X(...) into the factory and a field write into the setter.
finish: port.jar-links.every-update up from 5,302 of 9,149 with no update lower, and every linked standalone mod loading on a real 1.21.1 -> 1.21.2 server
wrongIf: an update's count drops, or a mod that links only through a learned replacement fails on the server because of it
